text: Others ran, out of breath, with heavy bags. I stood at rest on the travelator, bags at my feet, and moved faster than all of them.
explanation:
Joseph Prince received the theme for 2022 in a dream. He was in an airport on a moving walkway. All around him people were rushing, anxious, sprinting with heavy luggage. He had bags too, and they were heavy, but they rested on the travelator beside him. He was calm, and yet he was accelerating.

Rest and acceleration sound like opposites. In God's ways they belong together. "Come to Me… and I will give you rest" can be read, "I Myself will rest you." Your burdens don't disappear, but you don't have to carry them in your own strength. Enter His rest, and things that would have taken years can come to pass quickly.

text: "The plowman shall overtake the reaper." Sowing and harvest so close together, they run into each other.
explanation:
In Israel, wheat fields are ploughed in autumn and harvested months later in spring. The ploughman and the reaper never meet. But God says that when He rebuilds "the tabernacle of David, which has fallen down," the harvest will still be coming in when it's time to plough again, and "the treader of grapes [shall overtake] him who sows seed. The mountains shall drop sweet wine."

At the Jerusalem council, James quoted this very passage to explain the Gentiles coming to faith. God has been rebuilding David's tabernacle, His church, ever since. Expect acceleration: prayers answered, loved ones saved, healings springing forth speedily, and so much new wine that the tears of past years are swallowed up in joy.

text: "Among the sons of my father, He was pleased with me." It's one thing to be loved by God. It's another to be liked by Him.
explanation:
David told Israel's leaders that God chose Judah, then his father's house, "and among the sons of my father, He was pleased with me to make me king." God called him "a man after My own heart." God loves all His children, but He was fond of David.

Why? Others in Scripture were quick to repent. What set David apart was a longing from boyhood to bring the ark, the place of God's presence, to the centre of Israel's life. The ark pictured Jesus. Whatever you do with God's beloved Son, God does with you. Honour Him, make Him central, and you'll find God delights in you.

text: The law was kept inside the ark, under the mercy seat. When men of Beth Shemesh lifted the lid to look in, they died.
explanation:
Inside the ark were three things that recalled Israel's rebellion: the pot of manna they despised, Aaron's rod that budded to end their murmuring, and the tablets of the law they broke. God covered them all with the mercy seat, where the blood was sprinkled. Paul says God set forth Jesus as a "propitiation," hilasterion, the same word the Greek Old Testament uses for the mercy seat.

When the Philistines returned the ark, men of Beth Shemesh lifted the lid to look inside, and judgment fell. Many believers do the same today, pulling the law back out from under the blood. Leave it covered. Mercy sits above the law.

text: Uzzah, whose name means strength, reached out to steady the ark. God's glory doesn't need man's hand to hold it up.
explanation:
David put the ark on a new cart, the way the Philistines had, instead of on the shoulders of the Levites as God had commanded. When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah stretched out his hand, and he died. David named the place Perez-uzzah: perez means breach. It was the first breach in David's story.

The Levites had carried the ark on their shoulders through forty years in the wilderness, and no one had died. God's way brings life; man's inventions bring breaches. The problem at Perez wasn't sin. It was human strength intruding on God's work. Lay down your own effort and let Him carry what's His.

text: "The Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired it." There He promises, "I will abundantly bless her provision."
explanation:
David recalls hearing of the ark as a boy in Ephrathah, then finding it "in the fields of the woods": Kiriath-jearim, "city of the woods," where it sat neglected for twenty years. "Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength."

Then God speaks: "This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it. I will abundantly bless her provision." The word for desire speaks of an intense longing, and "abundantly bless" repeats the Hebrew verb to double it. God didn't choose Sinai, the mountain of demand. He chose Zion, the mountain of grace, and there He supplies.

text: "As Jesus has no eating disorder and no fear of what's ahead, so am I." After 30 years, she ate in peace the next day.
explanation:
A woman in Virginia had struggled with bulimia since the age of twelve. Every meal felt like a gun to her throat. Hospitalizations and recovery programs hadn't changed it. Then she began listening to grace-based teaching every day. One night she meditated on "as He is, so are we in this world" and said, "Jesus isn't worried about what to eat, and He doesn't hate His body. Neither do I." She asked God to help her receive it, and stopped all her efforts to control the disorder.

The next day every meal felt normal, without anxiety, and she has stayed free. That's rest and acceleration together: when you stop striving and receive who you are in Him, freedom can come faster than you ever imagined.
